issues.description: The problem specification and UML define a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void in SealSaloon, but the provided reference implementation declares checkOrderReady(boolean) with a boolean parameter and orderMeal calls checkOrderReady(true). This parameter mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about the expected method signature and whether a boolean parameter is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the SealSaloon.checkOrderReady method match the specification by removing the boolean parameter (declare public void checkOrderReady()). Update any internal calls (e.g., orderMeal) to call the no-argument method. If logging behavior is desired, implement it via an internal flag or a separate private method, but keep the public API consistent with the UML and problem description.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void, but the solution implementation provides checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). This signature mismatch (presence of a boolean parameter) breaks the direct mapping from the requirement to the implemented API and may confuse students who are asked to implement and call checkOrderReady() with no parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument checkOrderReady() method in the solution to match the problem specification. For example, add: public void checkOrderReady() { checkOrderReady(true); } and keep the existing checkOrderReady(boolean) as an internal/overloaded helper, or change the existing method to public void checkOrderReady() and incorporate logging control another way.
